candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel limit types (effluent Ce, instream waste concentrations derived via 2.13*Ce and related Cd columns, and separate Domestic/Irrigation/Livestock&Wildlife/Acute Aquatic/Chronic Aquatic/Human Health criteria columns). Which column is treated as the enforceable numeric discharge limit for a given parameter and monitoring period changes limit selection and exceedance comparison.

MQL values establish method quantitation limits for each pollutant. Interpretation of whether reported measurements below MQL are comparable to numeric limits, treated as qualified results, or excluded from compliance comparison changes exceedance determinations and missing-evidence classification.

The acute aquatic instream waste concentration column is labeled as a formula of effluent concentration rather than a standalone numeric criterion. Whether this formula defines the operative limit, supplements separate Acute Aquatic Criteria values, or is informational only changes the applicable numeric limit used for comparison.

This row simultaneously presents an effluent Ce value (10), calculated instream waste concentrations (21.3, 0.49862059, etc.), and distinct criteria-column values (Domestic 1, Acute Aquatic 19, Chronic 15, Human Health 30). Different choices of which field is the enforceable effluent limit change compliance outcomes for reported measurements.

The effluent Ce field is blank while instream waste columns show 0 and Domestic Criteria shows 70. Interpretation of blank Ce versus zero instream values versus the nonzero Domestic Criteria column determines whether an enforceable limit exists, which limit applies, and how missing or below-quantitation results are classified.

Many criteria cells use the sentinel value 1E+100. Whether this denotes no applicable criterion, a non-operative placeholder, or an effectively unbounded limit changes which criteria column governs and whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for that parameter and endpoint.

Irrigation and Livestock&Wildlife criteria are marked N/A while Acute Aquatic, Chronic Aquatic, and Human Health retain numeric values. Whether N/A means the criterion is absent and non-operative versus meaning something different from the 1E+100 sentinel used elsewhere changes which limits are considered enforceable for this parameter.

This row lacks an MQL value while presenting zeros in instream columns and numeric Acute/Chronic aquatic criteria (28, 6.6). Interpretation of the missing MQL, blank Ce, and zero instream entries affects detection/comparison rules, whether monitoring for this parameter is required, and how absent or non-numeric results are categorized.

The Need TMDL column appears for each pollutant and is uniformly marked N/A in this segment. Whether N/A means no TMDL-based limit or monitoring obligation applies, versus indicating an unresolved TMDL assessment, changes which numeric limits and monitoring requirements are treated as operative.

This grouping label separates a subset of pollutants within the table. Interpretation of whether BASE/NEUTRAL denotes a distinct monitoring suite, analytical method group, or conditional applicability category changes which monitoring requirements are considered applicable for listed parameters.
